title: The cypress tree
hookLine: asked why Bodhidharma came, Zhaozhou answers: the cypress tree in the garden (Gateless Gate 37)
last: NO LINE BETWEEN HOLY AND PLAIN.

cards: Three days ago, a man hung from a tree by his teeth while someone asked why Bodhidharma came from the west. Today the question comes back, and this time it gets an answer.
A monk puts it to Zhaozhou, the old Chan teacher you first met with his answer mu: why did Bodhidharma come from the west? Zhaozhou doesn't lecture or open a book.
He points, as it were, out the window: the cypress tree in front of the garden. Case thirty-seven of the Gateless Gate is that short.

teach.b: First, the question. Tradition says Bodhidharma carried the Chan way from India to China, so asking why he came is asking what the whole tradition is for.
It's the question the man in the tree was asked, and here a teacher answers it. Second, the answer.
Zhaozhou names a tree in a courtyard, right there. Not a symbol, not a parable: a tree you could walk over and touch. Like the flax, it won't send the monk somewhere else for the meaning.
The answer to the big question is standing in the yard. Third, a detail for the curious.
The Chinese word names a cypress or juniper kind of tree, and some English versions call it an oak. So depending on your book, Zhaozhou points at a different tree.

The koan doesn't seem to mind; whatever is in front of you is the point. Fourth, why it lands. Some questions in a life seem to need a faraway answer: a different job, a different city, a different self.
The tree was there before the question and will be there after it.
In koan practice, the student isn't asked for an essay on trees, but to meet the tree, or whatever is in front of them, so fully that nothing is left over to explain.

how: In Rinzai Zen training this case is given as a koan, and students carry the phrase 'the cypress tree in front of the garden' through sitting and work until they can present it to the teacher.

games.why: Zhaozhou says: the cypress tree in front of the garden. the answer was standing in the yard.

practice: Find one tree, out a window, down the street, or one you know well in memory, and look at it: the bark, the way the branches split, where the light hits.
Don't name its species or think about what it stands for; just let it be a tree, in front of you, now. When the mind wanders, come back to the tree and breathe with it.

wordCard.voice: The cypress tree. Zhaozhou's answer when asked why Bodhidharma came from the west, case thirty-seven of the Gateless Gate: the tree in front of the garden. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese: 'the cypress tree in front of the garden'. 柏 names a cypress or juniper. Pronunciation approximates Mandarin.

carryVoice: Your line: the cypress in the garden. The answer was standing in the yard all along. That's today, done.
